title: Swimmer Ollie Morgan Is Winning Medals Again
summary:
Swimmer Ollie Morgan says moving to Manchester has helped him win medals again. The 23-year-old from Bishop's Castle in Shropshire swam for Team GB at the 2024 Olympics. He broke a British record on his way to the 100m backstroke final. But he calls this a 'challenging year', with injuries and a move to a new training base.

The medals tell a happier story. Morgan won five silver medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow in July. One of them was in the men's 200m backstroke. Now he wants more success at next month's World Aquatics Championships in China.

Morgan says training in Manchester is the key. 'I'm now training day in, day out with Olympic champions,' he said. 'Racing with them day in, day out has brought the enjoyment back for me.'

There is one tricky part. The next championships will be swum in a short 25m pool in Beijing, not the 50m pools he is used to. So Morgan has been working hard on his starts and turns. 'It's about putting yourself in situations you're uncomfortable with,' he said.
why_it_matters: It shows that practising with people better than you can help you enjoy a sport again and get better at it.
